title: Trivia with a Whore, Part 1
summary: Delilah, using a chosen on-air name and the self-description `erotic provider`, gives a long first-person account of entering sex work in her late thirties, learning through stripping, webcam work, advertising, early appointments, fetish training, client screening and boundary enforcement. The cast mixes that career history with medical folklore, racial and gender stereotypes, an alleged review-site coercion story, explicit fetish discussion and a white-elephant trivia game. The final hour turns a consensual private meeting between Delilah and Steve into a production ethics test: the room repeatedly tries to listen, moves a microphone, sends people toward the door and admits the pair may not know they are being monitored. Every idea remains represented; factual corrections, attribution, consent analysis and narrow public privacy restrictions remain separate from the transcript.
source_notes: The raw file contains 4,120 segments and approximately 26,463 words; the machine-clean file contains 4,094 segments and approximately 26,459 words across 9,021.56 seconds.

The cleaner logs twenty-four empty artifacts and eight short repeated outro runs. The empty drops are valid. The repeated `We love you, girl` chorus is plausible musical speech and requires audio verification rather than automatic deletion.

California Penal Code section 647(b) defines prostitution to include a lewd act for money or other consideration and separately addresses soliciting, agreeing and engaging. The hosts' `technically illegal` and `trading content` labels are therefore not legal conclusions: https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=PEN&sectionNum=647

NCI places the prostate below the bladder, in front of the rectum, and describes digital rectal examination as palpation for abnormalities. It does not support the episode's claim that men normally ejaculate during the exam: https://www.cancer.gov/types/prostate/understanding-prostate-changes

The guest's LA Weekly reference is most consistent with Dennis Romero's `Porn Defends the Money Shot`, which discusses escorting, condoms and a website describing its subject as an adult-film star, escort, domina and webcam fetishist: https://www.laweekly.com/porn-defends-the-money-shot/

NFL records Super Bowl XLVIII as Seattle Seahawks versus Denver Broncos on February 2, 2014. The `yesterday` trivia answer places this recording on or near February 3, 2014, independent of archive release metadata: https://www.nfl.com/news/super-bowl-xlviii-faq-everything-you-need-to-know-0ap2000000317294
The episode itself is primary for Delilah's terminology, career narrative and boundaries. The hosts' numerical estimates, stereotypes, legal euphemisms and guesses are not promoted to facts.

The episode's offensive, explicit, coercive, implausible, contradictory and wrong ideas remain intact. Restrictions protect private clients, relatives, minors, homes, intimate sounds and a secondhand assault survivor; they do not censor ideas.
speaker_policy: The ensemble is contextually recognizable, but this episode has no accepted identity windows or independently held-out multispeaker validation. Named dialogue remains withheld.

connections.why: The hosts' euphemisms should be read against the statute's focus on compensated lewd acts and other consideration, not as legal advice.
Watching part of one episode does not authorize all downstream indexing or intimate surveillance.
Clinical anatomy supports location and examination, not instant-ejaculation folklore or orientation claims.
The episode gives an unusually detailed first-person sequence from bar work to webcam work, ads, appointments and fetish specialization.
AOL, Adult FriendFinder, Match.com and TER locate the story in an early-web market transition.
Stalking, home exposure, managers, cameras, drivers and the ability to end sessions recur as practical safety infrastructure.
Her first website trade foreshadows the episode's later attempt to label an intimate encounter `trading content`.
A clinical term becomes a vehicle for unsupported endocrine, chromosome and racial claims.
The film prompts a discussion of review power and sexual coercion.
